description: Procedure for addressing a systematic increase in false rejection rate from the vision inspection system, covering calibration target condition, lens cleanliness, lighting stability, camera mounting, and recalibration.

box_1.text: Record the false rejection rate over the last 100 parts and the rejection type (orientation, marking, presence). Compare with the baseline false rejection rate from the last successful calibration.

box_2.text: Is the false rejection limited to one inspection type (e.g. only orientation rejections or only marking rejections)?

box_3.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Access the vision rejection log and sort by inspection module. 2. Identify which module produces the highest proportion of false rejects. 3. Check whether the rejections correlate with a specific part feature.

box_4.text: Is the calibration target in good condition (no surface scratches, discolouration, or contamination)?

box_5.text: Inspect the calibration target for surface contamination, scratches, or colour fading. Verify that the target geometry is intact and undamaged.

box_6.text: Clean the calibration target with an approved optical cleaning cloth. If the target is scratched or faded beyond the acceptable condition limit, replace it.

box_7.text: Is the camera lens clean and free of contamination?

box_8.text: Inspect the camera lens for dust, oil, or condensation. Verify that the lens protective cover is intact.

box_9.text: Clean the camera lens with an approved optical cloth and lens cleaner. rerun ten test inspections with known good reference parts and measure the false rejection rate.

box_10.text: Is the ambient lighting at the inspection station stable and within the specification range?

box_11.text: Check the inspection station lighting shielding for gaps. Measure the background illumination level at the camera field using a lux meter and compare against the maximum ambient specification.

box_12.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Measure the ambient light level at the inspection window with a lux meter. 2. Compare against the maximum permitted ambient illuminance. 3. Check the camera mount for looseness or detectable vibration.

box_13.text: Is the camera securely mounted with no detectable vibration induced movement?

box_14.text: Check the camera mounting bracket fastener torque and verify that no vibration is transmitted to the camera from the machine frame during a live production cycle.

box_15.text: Tighten the camera mounting fasteners and add vibration isolation if required. rerun ten inspection cycles and measure the false rejection rate.

box_16.text: Has the false rejection rate returned to within the acceptable baseline threshold after corrections?

box_17.text: Run the full vision system calibration procedure using the calibration target and update all calibration parameters. Notify the maintenance team.

box_18.text: Refer to the vision system calibration procedure.

box_19.text: Is the false rejection rate within the acceptable threshold after recalibration?

box_20.text: Escalate to the maintenance team: the vision system false rejection rate cannot be corrected through recalibration; inspect camera sensor and optics for physical damage.

box_21.text: Record the recalibration date, corrective actions, and final false rejection rate in the quality log. Notify quality assurance team.

box_23.text: Has the false rejection rate reached a level that indicates a vision system failure, where genuine conforming parts are being systematically rejected and production viability is compromised?

box_24.text: End, vision system shut down immediately: false rejection rate critical, quarantine parts rejected in the affected window and escalate to vision system engineer

box_25.text: Vision system lens and focus diagnostic (GRAPH 37)
